title: unique_ptr and handing over ownership
description:
`std::unique_ptr` is a pointer that deletes what it points at when it goes out of scope. There is exactly one owner at a time; ownership can be **moved** but never copied.

Using the `Player` struct provided, write:

- `std::unique_ptr<Player> makePlayer(std::string name, int level)` using `std::make_unique`.
- a class `Team` with
  - `void add(std::unique_ptr<Player> player)`: the team takes ownership (store it in a `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Player>>`; you will need `std::move`),
  - `std::size_t size() const`,
  - `const Player& at(std::size_t index) const`,
  - `int totalLevel() const`.

There is no `new` and no `delete` anywhere, and nothing can leak.
hints: `return std::make_unique<Player>(Player{ std::move(name), level });` (or the struct's constructor) creates the player.
A `unique_ptr` cannot be copied, so `add` takes it by value and stores it with `m_players.push_back(std::move(player));`. `at` returns `*m_players[index]`.
